extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in wartime/current events (WWII-era)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing concise, datelined news dispatches and human-interest items from wartime fronts that combine official communiqués, multiple dispatches, tactical details, casualty figures, and personal accounts for a general readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution to official spokesmen and communiqués
rubrics_metrics.description: Use explicit attribution for major claims (e.g., "An official spokesman announced that General Sir Bernard L. Montgomery’s forces had 'penetrated the Enfidaville position,' and that 'heavy fighting continues.'").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor reporting what 'official spokesmen', 'Allied headquarters', or named commands announce; quote their phrasing for key operational claims so readers know the source and authority of the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple dispatches and geographically distributed sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate reports and dispatches from different locations (Allied Headquarters in North Africa, Malta, Cairo, London, etc.) to build the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite dispatches from Malta, Cairo, London, and local correspondents to corroborate events and provide different angles (air, land, naval).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report enemy claims and note possible exaggeration
rubrics_metrics.description: Include opposing broadcasts or communiqués and indicate their reliability (e.g., Berlin broadcast calling Allied claims 'at least exaggerated if not completely incorrect').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present enemy statements but flag them (use phrases like 'claimed', 'announced', or cite broadcasts) and offer context or counter-evidence when available to avoid repeating unverified propaganda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specific military details (units, locations, tactics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Name armies, divisions, groups, precise positions, and tactics: Eighth Army, Enfidaville position, moonlight assault, attack sectors, unit names like the Fifty-seventh Fighter Group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete operational details (unit designations, geographic points, and tactics) so the reader understands who is fighting where and how; explain unfamiliar tactics (e.g., moonlight attacks) briefly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative reporting of losses and materiel
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply numbers and time frames for casualties, aircraft destroyed, bombs dropped (e.g., '112 Axis planes in 48 hours', '2,000,000 pounds of bombs in the week of April 10-17').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report figures with the period covered and the reporting source; where totals differ among sources, present both and attribute each number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual strategic analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain operational context and expectations (e.g., 'no decisive results could be expected for some time', 'infantry must fight for each foot of ground').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide readers with broader tactical/strategic perspective — terrain difficulty, expected pace of advance, and how current actions fit into larger campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-interest profiles and personal anecdotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include short humanizing pieces about individuals (e.g., wounded Capt. Dallas wanting ice cream and phone calls; profiles of pilots who became aces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weave personal stories and direct quotes into reporting to add emotional resonance and illustrate consequences for individuals amid broader military events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid, descriptive language to convey action
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ evocative descriptions and metaphors (e.g., 'transports tumbled out of the sky like leaves in a forest fire', 'shattering power' of the air offensive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance vivid phrasing with factual accuracy to make accounts compelling without overstating or misrepresenting events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include definitional or explanatory notes for readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain technical or cultural points (e.g., 'Five victories make a pilot an ace') so lay readers can follow significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add brief parenthetical explanations or side notes when introducing military conventions, unit roles, or unusual terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signal uncertainty and avoid implying absence of action
rubrics_metrics.description: When information is scarce or withheld (reticence in communiqués), explicitly note that silence does not mean inaction ('this reticence did not necessarily indicate that fighting was not going on').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cautionary language to avoid false negatives; tell readers when reports are limited and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report political and civilian developments alongside military news
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover parallel political events and civilian conditions (e.g., Algerian Councils General debating French provisional government, lend-lease supplies in Morocco, civilian food relief efforts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the diplomatic/political context and effects on local populations to give a fuller picture of the campaign's consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute moral tone and propaganda value where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Note the propaganda or morale impact of actions and supplies (e.g., lend-lease sugar's 'propaganda effect' and 'brighten the heart' teasers in Army papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out when information or actions serve morale/propaganda functions and identify the source of such messaging (Army papers, broadcasts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine frontline dispatches with shorter topical items
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a modular page structure: long dispatches on major operations plus shorter items (aircraft tallies, personal vignettes, supply reports) under subheadings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize content into datelined lead stories and subsidiary short pieces to cover multiple facets of the campaign while keeping each piece focused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite awards, ranks, and honors as relevant human-interest detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention medals and promotions (Distinguished Service Cross, Distinguished Flying Cross) when profiling personnel to indicate significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include such identifiers to convey status and credibility of individuals, but ensure accuracy of titles and dates.
